record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: For polymers with partly attractive but stable small interactions, prove that they scale to Brownian motion in dimensions greater than 4, and determine whether phase transitions exist when the interaction is stable but attractive.

evidence.quote: Polymers with partly attractive interactions: prove that they scale to Brownian motion in d > 4, at least if the interaction is stable and small. Existence of transitions when the interaction is stable but attractive?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a discrete-time simple random walk model of a self-interacting polymer in $\mathbb{Z}^d$. For an $n$-step nearest-neighbor path $\omega = (\omega_0, \omega_1, \ldots, \omega_n)$ starting at the origin, define a Hamiltonian
$$H_n(\omega) = \sum_{0 \le i < j \le n} V(\omega_j - \omega_i),$$
where $V : \mathbb{Z}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ is a (possibly sign-changing) two-body interaction potential that is "stable" in the sense that there exists a constant $B \ge 0$ such that $H_n(\omega) \ge -B n$ for every $n$ and every path $\omega$. Assume the negative (attractive) part of $V$ is nonzero, so that the interaction is partly attractive, but that $V$ is small (e.g., multiplied by a sufficiently small coupling constant $\beta > 0$).

Let $P_n$ denote the uniform measure on $n$-step simple random walk paths, and define the polymer measure
$$\mu_n(d\omega) = \frac{1}{Z_n} \exp(-H_n(\omega)) \, P_n(d\omega), \quad Z_n = E_{P_n}[\exp(-H_n)].$$
Let $X^{(n)}(t) := \omega_{\lfloor nt \rfloor} / \sqrt{n}$, $t \in [0,1]$, be the diffusively rescaled path.

(a) Prove that for $d > 4$ and for stable, partly attractive interactions with a sufficiently small coupling constant, the law of $X^{(n)}$ under $\mu_n$ converges weakly to a (nondegenerate) Brownian motion on $[0,1]$.

(b) For stable but partly attractive interactions of arbitrary strength, determine whether there exists a phase transition (in the coupling constant or in an inverse temperature parameter) separating a diffusive Brownian-scaling phase from a collapsed/localized phase, and characterize such transitions when they occur.
artifact.status_search_result: Diffusive (Brownian) scaling has been established in several related polymer models with weak interactions in high dimensions (e.g., weak-disorder directed polymers, semi-directed polymers in random environment for $d \ge 4$ at high temperature, and charged polymers in the delocalized regime). For specific attractive models such as the quenched charged-polymer model of Garel–Orland, a first-order transition between Brownian scaling and four-point localization has been proven. However, the general statement for arbitrary stable, partly attractive small two-body interactions in $d > 4$, together with a complete characterization of phase transitions in the attractive stable regime, remains open in this generality.

status_evidence.title: Charged polymers in the attractive regime: a first order transition from Brownian scaling to four points localization
status_evidence.snippet: Below the critical inverse temperature the polymer is delocalized... the rescaled trajectory converges to the Brownian path... At the critical inverse temperature, the maximum time spent at points jumps discontinuously...
status_evidence.claim: For a specific attractive (charged) polymer model, Brownian scaling in the delocalized phase and a first-order transition to a localized phase have been proven, illustrating partial progress on the general question.

status_evidence.title: On the phase diagram of the polymer model
status_evidence.snippet: Phase transitions between weak and strong disorder regimes; in weak disorder the polymer behaves diffusively like Brownian motion.
status_evidence.claim: Diffusive scaling in high dimensions and weak coupling is known for related polymer models, supporting partial-solved status.

status_evidence.title: The statistical mechanics of stretched polymers
status_evidence.snippet: Characterization of critical force and order of phase transition in the attractive case, with proofs of diffusivity in dimensions 4 and higher at high temperature for semi-directed polymers.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results are available for the existence and order of phase transitions in attractive polymer models.
